title: Countable n-rectifiability is preserved by the inverse similarity
statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, ξ ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0 and M ⊆ ℝ^N. Suppose M is countably n-rectifiable in the sense of Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable: there are a set M₀ ⊆ ℝ^N with H^n(M₀) = 0 (H^n = μHE[n]) and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^N (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n). Then σ^{-1}(M) = {y ∈ ℝ^N : ξ + t·y ∈ M} is countably n-rectifiable, where σ(y) := ξ + t·y.
lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (ξ : Euclidean N) (t : ℝ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)), 0 < t → Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M → Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n ((fun y : Euclidean N ↦ ξ + t • y) ⁻¹' M)
